providers.title: Cocycles are gradients
providers.scope: On the Cayley complex of a presentation, every 1-cochain with values in an abelian group whose integral around every cell vanishes is the gradient of a function, unique up to a constant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The space of finite-energy gradients
providers.scope: The gradients of finite-energy functions form a closed subspace of the square-summable functions on the edges.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Constant at infinity
providers.scope: A finite-energy function that tends to a constant at infinity has its gradient in the closure of the gradients of finitely supported functions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Interaction of two cuts
providers.scope: For two finite-energy functions, the number of pairs of equal or cell-sharing edges in their cuts at levels s and t has integral at most D times the product of the gradient norms; so it is finite for almost every pair of levels.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A function with connected level sides
providers.scope: If the finite-energy gradients are not all limits of gradients of finitely supported functions, there is a finite-energy function with values in [0,1], not tending to a constant at infinity, whose level sides at regular levels are connected and whose level cuts are dually connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Good boxes exist
providers.scope: Every neighbourhood of a point of the base cube contains a box around the point whose endpoint levels are regular and whose endpoint cuts interact in finitely many pairs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finitely many components
providers.scope: The vertex set of a good box has finitely many connected components.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Localized functions
providers.scope: The margin of a box times the indicator of one of its components has finite energy, and its cuts lie in shifted cuts of the functions defining the box.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The compact space
providers.scope: The closure of the profiles is a compact metrizable space in which the group is a dense set of isolated points and on which it acts by homeomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Square summable edge lengths
providers.scope: In the weighted metric the lengths of the edges of the Cayley graph are square summable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The boundary is a continuum
providers.scope: For a one-ended Cayley graph with finite-energy gradients beyond the closure of the finitely supported ones, the boundary is compact, connected and has more than one point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Paths near a boundary point
providers.scope: Every neighbourhood of a boundary point contains a smaller one any two of whose vertices are joined by a graph path inside the larger.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Virtually cyclic groups are not one-ended
providers.scope: A finitely generated group with an infinite cyclic subgroup of finite index has a Cayley graph with at least two infinite components after removing a finite set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Translated cut lengths
providers.scope: The integral over all levels of the total translated length near a level cut of a finite-energy function is finite and tends to zero as the translating element leaves finite sets.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Collapse of translated cuts
providers.scope: Along a subsequence of group elements converging to a boundary point, the translated ends of almost every level cut of finitely many coordinates converge uniformly to that point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Convergence
providers.scope: If group elements converge to a boundary point a and their inverses to b, they map every closed set avoiding b into any neighbourhood of a, for almost all terms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Convergence group
providers.scope: The group acts on the boundary as a convergence group, and the boundary is infinite.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Parabolic comparison
providers.scope: For a parabolic fixed point p, the distance between g and gp tends to zero as g leaves finite sets.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dense orbits
providers.scope: If the group is torsion-free, every orbit in the boundary is dense.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Thin walls
providers.scope: For almost every level, the set of boundary points at which a level cut accumulates is covered by finitely many sets of arbitrarily small total diameter.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dimension of the boundary
providers.scope: The finite-energy boundary of a one-ended group has covering dimension at most one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: First Čech cohomology of the boundary
providers.scope: If every 1-cochain on the Cayley complex with finitely supported coboundary can be corrected by a finitely supported cochain, the first Čech cohomology of the boundary vanishes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No circles; cut points
providers.scope: Under these assumptions the boundary contains no simple closed curve, and it is locally connected only if it is a dendrite with cut points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A graph on the cut points
providers.scope: On the cut points of the boundary there is a connected graph with finitely many orbits of edges whose edges join cut points with a common neighbour in the tree of cut points; it induces a connected graph on the cut points next to a fixed vertex of the tree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Paths of cut points near a point
providers.scope: Two sequences of cut points converging to the same boundary point are joined by paths of cut points in the graph that converge to that point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A block of the boundary
providers.scope: The closure of the set of cut points next to a vertex of the tree that is not a cut point is a retract of the boundary by a map that is locally constant outside it; it is a compact connected space with more than one point, without cut points, of dimension at most one, with vanishing first Čech cohomology when that of the boundary vanishes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A continuum without cut points and its graph
providers.scope: For the boundary without cut points, and for a block of a boundary with cut points: a compact connected space without cut points of dimension at most one, a subgroup acting on it with the convergence property, and a connected graph with finitely many orbits whose vertices accumulate on the space, with paths near each point of the space.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Component labels
providers.scope: After deleting a set of vertices of the graph, each point of the continuum at which deleted vertices do not accumulate has a component of the remaining graph that contains all remaining vertices near it; this label is locally constant.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A system of annuli
providers.scope: There is an invariant set of pairs of disjoint closed sets in which only finitely many members have two sides of diameter above a given bound, and which contains chains of every length from a closed set to a neighbourhood of any point of the continuum outside it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Annular depth
providers.scope: The largest length of a chain of annuli from a set to a point is invariant under the group, finite between group elements, and at least any given number near every point of the continuum outside a closed set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Translates that shrink to a point
providers.scope: If the depths of group elements measured from a closed set tend to infinity, then along a subsequence the translates of the set by their inverses lie in arbitrarily small balls around one point of the continuum.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A comparison of depths
providers.scope: The depth from such a translate to a group element away from the limit point is at least the depth to the identity plus the depth from the identity to the element, minus a constant that depends only on the distance from the limit point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deleted vertices after a translation
providers.scope: In a compact set away from the limit point, the vertices whose translates are deleted at the next depth lie in one finite set for all large indices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Labels after a translation
providers.scope: After translation by an element of large depth, any two points of the continuum other than the limit point have the same component label at the next depth, for all large indices.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Majority labels
providers.scope: Beyond one depth, for every group element of that depth two of the three points of the translated three-point set have the same component label at the next depth, and this majority label does not change under right multiplication by an element of a given finite set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One threshold for all larger depths
providers.scope: Beyond one depth, two points of the continuum outside the closed set with equal component labels at a depth have equal labels at the next depth.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Limit points of chains
providers.scope: In a compact metric space, if finite chains of points have steps tending to zero and their first and last points converge, the set of their limit points is closed and connected and contains both limits.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The continuum is locally connected
providers.scope: A compact connected space without cut points with a group, a graph and the properties (S1) to (S7) is locally connected.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first Čech cohomology of the boundary does not vanish
providers.scope: In both cases of the lesson on a continuum without cut points and its graph, the first Čech cohomology of the boundary with coefficients in the group with two elements is not zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite-energy gradients are limits
providers.scope: For a triangular presentation with a one-ended Cayley graph, without elements of finite order, with the cochain condition for the group with two elements, and such that the group fixes a point of the dendrite quotient of the boundary whenever the boundary has cut points, every finite-energy gradient is a limit of gradients of finitely supported functions.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
